description: Building robot software with the Robot Operating System: the node graph and architecture, publish-subscribe topics and messages, request-reply services and long-running actions, coordinate-frame transforms, simulation, perception pipelines, and the tools for launching and debugging a running robot. Practised entirely in the browser against a simulated robot and sensors, with no physical hardware required.
modelledOn: Quigley, Gerkey and Smart, Programming Robots with ROS
Siciliano and Khatib, Springer Handbook of Robotics
outcomes: Design a robot application as a graph of cooperating nodes with clear responsibilities and interfaces.
Implement publishers, subscribers, services and action servers and choose the right communication pattern for a task.
Model a robot's links and sensors with coordinate frames and transform data correctly between them.
Run and inspect a robot in simulation, driving it and reading its sensors without physical hardware.
Assemble a perception pipeline that turns sensor streams into usable world information.
Launch, parameterise, record and debug a multi-node robot system and diagnose failures from its logs.

units.title: Robots and robot software architecture
topics: What a robot is: sensing, computation and actuation; the sense-plan-act loop and reactive versus deliberative control
Why robot software is a distributed system: many processes, asynchronous messages, partial failure
ROS as a framework: the computation graph, the master or discovery layer, and the reasons for a message-passing design
The robotics software ecosystem and where ROS fits; versions and long-term support
Setting up a browser-based ROS workspace, building packages and running a first node

units.title: Nodes, topics and messages
topics: Nodes as units of computation; naming, namespaces and the parameter server
Publish-subscribe over topics: decoupling producers and consumers, many-to-many communication
Message types and interface definition; standard messages for sensors, geometry and diagnostics
Defining custom messages; serialisation and message versioning pitfalls
Queue size, latching, publish rate and the cost of dropped or stale messages
Inspecting the graph with command-line tools: listing topics, echoing messages, measuring rates

units.title: Services and actions
topics: Request-reply services for short synchronous queries; service definitions and blocking calls
When a service is wrong: long tasks, cancellation, progress feedback
Action servers and clients: goals, feedback and results for navigate-to-goal and grasp tasks
Pre-emption, cancelling and goal state machines
Choosing between topics, services and actions for a given interaction

units.title: Transforms and coordinate frames
topics: Rigid-body pose: translation and rotation, rotation matrices, quaternions and Euler angles
The frame tree: base, odometry, map, sensor and end-effector frames; parent-child relationships
Broadcasting and buffering transforms over time; looking up a transform at a timestamp
Static versus dynamic transforms; extrinsic sensor calibration
Transforming a point, a laser scan or a detected object between frames
Diagnosing a broken or disconnected frame tree

units.title: Simulation of robots
topics: Why simulate: safety, cost, repeatability, and the reality gap for teams without hardware
Robot description: links, joints, inertia, collision and visual geometry in a URDF model
Spawning a robot in a simulated world with gravity, contact and sensor plugins
Simulated sensors: cameras, depth, lidar and IMU, and the noise models that make them realistic
Driving the simulated robot by publishing velocity commands and reading joint states

units.title: Perception pipelines
topics: From raw sensor stream to decision: the stages of a perception pipeline and their data types
Images: encoding, rectification, and converting between image messages and processing buffers
Point clouds and laser scans: filtering, downsampling and segmentation
Detecting and localising objects and publishing them as poses in the correct frame
Time synchronisation of multiple sensor streams and approximate-time matching
Visualising sensor data and pipeline output to confirm correctness

units.title: Launching, configuring and recording systems
topics: Launch files: starting many nodes, setting parameters, remapping names and composing subsystems
Parameters and configuration files for reusable, deployable robot stacks
Recording and replaying message logs to debug offline and build repeatable tests
Namespacing and multi-robot launches on one graph
Lifecycle and managed nodes; bringing a system up in a known order

units.title: Debugging and introspecting robot systems
topics: Logging levels and structured log output; reading a node's logs to localise a fault
Introspection tools: the node graph viewer, topic and transform inspectors, plotting over time
Common failures: no messages, wrong frame, clock and timestamp mismatch, queue overflow
Measuring latency and throughput and finding the bottleneck node
Diagnosing simulation artefacts under power-cut-interrupted sessions common on shared campus machines

units.title: Integrating a complete robot behaviour
topics: Composing nodes, transforms, perception and actions into one behaviour
A state machine or behaviour tree coordinating drive, sense and act
Parameterising the stack for a different simulated robot or world
Capstone: a simulated delivery robot that perceives an obstacle, plans around it and reports status over an action

schedule.title: Robots, ROS and the first node
schedule.exercise: Draw the sense-plan-act loop for a robot that follows a line, naming the sensors, the computation and the actuators.

tasks.title: Step through a sense-plan-act loop for a robot approaching a wall and mark where a reactive controller would respond faster than a planner
Create a workspace and a package in the browser environment, build it, and run a first node that prints a message every second
Split a single-script robot controller into three communicating processes, then simulate one process crashing and show how the rest of the system behaves

schedule.title: Nodes, topics and messages
schedule.exercise: Sketch the computation graph of a robot with a camera, a controller and a motor driver, labelling nodes and topics.

tasks.title: Write two nodes in different namespaces, read a parameter in each and print the full resolved node names
Write a publisher of distance readings and two subscribers, a logger and an obstacle warning, and verify both receive all 20 messages
Choose standard message types for a sensor, a velocity command and a diagnostic report, and write nodes that exchange all three correctly

schedule.title: Custom messages and graph inspection
schedule.exercise: Write a short note explaining why changing a message definition can break old recorded data and how you would version it.

tasks.title: Inspect a running graph to list its topics, echo one message stream and measure its publish rate in the visualiser
Define a custom battery status message, publish it from one node and subscribe to it in another, then check the decoded fields
Show the effect of queue size and publish rate on a slow subscriber, count dropped and stale messages, and tune settings to cut loss below 1 percent

schedule.title: Services and actions
schedule.exercise: List five robot interactions and decide in a table whether each should be a topic, a service or an action, with a reason.

tasks.title: Write a service that returns the current battery level and a client that calls it three times, with a timeout on the third call
Write an action server that moves a simulated robot to a goal with periodic feedback, and a client that prints progress and the final result
Draw and test the goal state machine of a navigate action, including a cancel request mid-way and a new goal pre-empting the old one

schedule.title: Poses and the frame tree
schedule.exercise: Convert a rotation of 90 degrees about the z axis into a rotation matrix and a quaternion by hand.

tasks.title: Convert five Euler angle triples into quaternions and rotation matrices with a script, and check that rotating a test vector gives the same result
Draw the frame tree for a mobile robot with base, odometry, map, lidar and camera frames, and mark the parent and child of each link
Broadcast a moving transform from odometry and look up the pose of the base in the map frame at three past timestamps

schedule.title: Transforms, calibration and diagnosis
schedule.exercise: Write the steps you would follow to find why two sensor readings do not line up in the same frame.

tasks.title: Add a static transform for a lidar mounted 20 cm forward and 15 cm up and check one reading point in the base frame
Transform a laser scan of 10 points and a detected object from the sensor frame into the map frame and verify against hand calculation
Find and repair a disconnected frame tree and a reversed parent-child pair in a given broken robot model, then confirm a lookup now succeeds

schedule.title: Simulation, URDF and sensors
schedule.exercise: Write a half-page argument for when simulation is enough and when real hardware tests are needed for a delivery robot.

tasks.title: Write a URDF description of a two-wheeled robot with links, joints and collision geometry, and print its link tree
Add a simulated lidar and camera with noise to a robot model, record 100 readings and compute their mean and spread
Drive a simulated robot in a square by publishing velocity commands, then measure the drift in pose and tune the commands to close the loop

schedule.title: Perception pipelines
schedule.exercise: Draw the stages and data types of a perception pipeline that finds a box on a table from a camera and a depth sensor.

tasks.title: Order six perception pipeline stages from raw stream to decision and label the data type that flows between each pair
Convert an image message to a pixel array, apply a threshold to find a coloured object, and report its bounding box
Filter and downsample a simulated point cloud, segment the floor plane, and report how many points remain on the object

schedule.title: Object localisation and synchronisation
schedule.exercise: Write a short note explaining why two sensors with slightly different clocks produce wrong fused positions and how matching helps.

tasks.title: Detect an object in a camera image and publish its pose as a stamped message in the camera frame
Synchronise image and lidar messages with approximate time matching, test with a 30 ms offset and count the matched pairs
Visualise a lidar scan, a detected object and the frame tree together, find the frame error that offsets the object, and fix it

schedule.title: Launch files, parameters and replay
schedule.exercise: Write a launch description listing the nodes, parameters and remappings needed to start a simulated robot with a different speed limit.

tasks.title: Write a launch file that starts three nodes, remaps a topic and sets a parameter, and check each node receives the right value
Move robot settings into a configuration file, load it for two robot profiles and verify the behaviours differ as intended
Record a 30 second message log from a simulated drive, replay it to a perception node and use it as a repeatable regression test

schedule.title: Multi-robot launches and lifecycle
schedule.exercise: Explain why bringing up a motor driver before its sensors are ready can be dangerous, and how a managed start sequence prevents it.

tasks.title: Launch two simulated robots under separate namespaces and verify their topics and frames do not collide
Bring up a managed node through its configure, activate and shutdown states and print the transition log
Design a start-up order for a camera, lidar, localisation and navigation stack using managed nodes, and test a failure in one dependency

schedule.title: Debugging and observability
schedule.exercise: Write a checklist of the first five things to check when a robot stops responding to velocity commands.

tasks.title: Add info, warning and error log messages with context to a node, filter them by level and find the cause of a seeded fault
Diagnose six faults in a simulated system, such as no messages, wrong frame, clock mismatch and queue overflow, and name the cause of each
Measure end-to-end latency and throughput along a four-node pipeline, find the bottleneck node and cut latency below a given target

schedule.title: Capstone: a delivery robot
schedule.exercise: Write a design note for a delivery robot that lists its nodes, interfaces, frames and failure behaviour, and a test plan.

tasks.title: Compose nodes for driving, sensing and reporting into one launchable behaviour in the simulator and run it for a full 60 second test
Implement a state machine or behaviour tree that coordinates drive, sense and act, and test it with five scripted obstacle cases
Build a simulated delivery robot that perceives an obstacle, plans around it and reports status over an action, and show that it passes five trials
